claims.explanation: Isoxsuprine is a beta-adrenergic agonist that also inhibits CDK1, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on CDK1 activity and/or beta-adrenergic signaling. TP53 mutation is nearly universal in sensitive lines, suggesting that loss of p53-mediated cell-cycle arrest or apoptosis sensitizes cells to CDK1 inhibition. Conversely, intact PTEN or NF1 may protect through PI3K/mTOR or RAS/MAPK-mediated survival signaling.

features.basis: Observed pattern: TP53 mutations in 19/20 sensitive lines vs 15/20 resistant lines; p53 loss may impair cell-cycle arrest after CDK1 inhibition.
Isoxsuprine inhibits CDK1 (IC50 2.9 µM); high CDK1 expression may increase dependence on CDK1 activity.
Observed pattern: PTEN mutations in 4/20 resistant lines vs 1/20 sensitive lines; PTEN loss may activate PI3K/AKT survival signaling.
Observed pattern: NF1 mutations in 4/20 resistant lines vs 1/20 sensitive lines; NF1 loss may activate RAS/MAPK survival signaling.
Isoxsuprine is an ADRB2 agonist; high ADRB2 expression may enhance downstream cAMP-mediated effects.
Observed pattern: BRAF mutations in 4/20 resistant lines vs 2/20 sensitive lines; BRAF mutation may drive MAPK survival.
Observed pattern: KRAS mutations in 4/20 resistant lines vs 2/20 sensitive lines; KRAS mutation may drive MAPK survival.
Observed pattern: EGFR mutations in 3/20 sensitive lines vs 0/20 resistant lines; EGFR mutation may increase dependence on survival signaling.
Observed pattern: PIK3CA mutations in 4/20 sensitive lines vs 1/20 resistant lines; PIK3CA mutation may increase dependence on PI3K signaling.
Observed pattern: CDKN2A mutations in 3/20 sensitive lines vs 1/20 resistant lines; CDKN2A loss may impair cell-cycle arrest.
Observed pattern: ATM mutations in 3/20 resistant lines vs 1/20 sensitive lines; ATM loss may impair DNA damage response.
Observed pattern: ARID1A mutations in 4/20 resistant lines vs 1/20 sensitive lines; ARID1A loss may alter chromatin and survival.
